decisions.reason: Attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1 (dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl per manifest-excerpt.json) whose install script runs node-gyp configure build and fails on missing Visual Studio/MSVC, citing specific gyp ERR! find VS lines from install-error.log; not blamed on pnpm/network.

Quotes lease-excerpt.md's top-level static `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'` and the note that the loader must load fs-ext even on Windows; explains --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install time to module-load time at boot, so it cannot achieve a working service.

Distinguishes Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW/WaitForSingleObject, 'no flock(2) is involved on Windows') from POSIX flock(2) via fs-ext, concludes fs-ext is dead code on Windows, and keeps real flock for non-Windows in the plan.

Follows the patches/node-pty precedent: pnpm patch fs-ext@2.1.1, skip node-gyp install only on win32, replace entry with a conditional loader giving an import-safe pure-JS fallback on Windows while non-Windows keeps the native build, register in pnpm-workspace.yaml patchedDependencies, reinstall, and verify install exit 0, module load, and service boot with semaphore lock.

Explicitly respects the no-Visual-Studio constraint; the patch lives only in the repo's patches/ dir with fs-ext on npm untouched; local patching of installed files is correctly framed as the allowed pnpm patch mechanism.
Cites full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and connects it to the gyp ERR! find VS fs-ext install failure and the win32 node-gyp-skip + pure-JS-fallback patch remedy, not merely echoing the id.

caps.reason: Plan never installs Visual Studio; it explicitly skips node-gyp on win32 and the corridor section affirms 'explicitly not installing Visual Studio'.
--ignore-scripts is analyzed and rejected; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via a patched pure-JS fallback, not script skipping.
Plan uses the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism; upstream fs-ext repository/npm package is explicitly untouched.
Windows keeps the named kernel semaphore lock unchanged; the stubbed flock is never called on Windows and POSIX keeps real flock — no weakened write ownership.
